metadata.case_name: CHAN YUK KING v. TUNG CHUN

injuries.description: Fracture of the coccyx / sacrococcygeal fracture (S4 fracture / acute traumatic angulation of the sacrococcygeal junction).
source: X-ray performed at the hospital shown there was a fracture of the coccyx.
The MRI scan taken on 18 March 2006 showed she had an S4 fracture(i.e. of the sacral segment).
the plaintiff's MRI and x-ray showed she had suffered from contusion with fracture of S4 or an acute traumatic angulation of the sacrococcygeal junction.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified fracture of lumbar spine or pelvis

manifestations.description: severe pain over her buttocks and her back immediately after the collision
pain and tenderness with stiffness over her back and buttocks, particularly with changes of the weather
pain after she walked for prolonged periods or sat for a prolonged period of time
pain when she carried heavy weights
off and on low back pain 3-4 times a week (reported at joint examination)
feels tired easily and her sleep had been disturbed
no lower limb pain, numbness or weaknesses (noted by doctors)

treatments_received: manipulation of the sacrococcygeal fracture under local anaesthesia

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: She no longer played tennis or badminton which she used to play once a week. She had also stopped hiking and ballroom dancing after the accident; she resumed swimming on advice.

losses.category: Loss of ability to give birth
losses.description: She claimed she was told the injury to the coccygeal region would affect child-bearing. She therefore did not get pregnant again after the accident, even though she had intended to have a child with her present husband before the accident.

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
losses.description: She would feel nervous crossing a busy road.
